Austin Filmmaker Chris McInroy Launches Medical Fundraiser

Campaign will assist comedy-horror mainstay recover after incident
by Richard Whittaker November 22, 2026November 22, 2026

If you’ve been to a film festival in Austin, or a genre festival anywhere around the world, the odds are good that you’ve seen a Chris McInroy short. Now the Austin filmmaker needs help after an incident that has left him in the ICU.

McInroy is known as the master of the comedy horror short and an integral member of Austin’s filmmaking community. He’s also become a fave among festival bookers, with the Fangoria Chainsaw Awards-nominated “Guts” premiering at Fantastic Fest, 2016’s “Death Metal” screening at South by Southwest, “We Joined a Cult” featured as part of Austin Horror Film Festival and “We Summoned a Demon” a hit at Other Worlds Austin. However, he’s not just a hometown hero, as his films have also been lauded and awarded at festivals around the country and internationally, as far afield as Sitges in Spain and Fantasia in Canada. He also created a segment for the Austin-made anthology, Scare Package, and has been working on his feature debut. His latest short, “Haunting of Play House,” received its Austin premiere during Fantastic Fest and will screen again this weekend as part of Horror for the Holidays’ film festival and competition.

Yet McInroy will not be in attendance, as he is currently recovering from a torn esophagus. He has undergone several procedures and will remain in the ICU until his doctors are happy with his progress. However, even after he is released from hospital, he will be facing an extended period of rehab and will be dependent on a feeding tube for the foreseeable future. His wife, Erin, is taking time to care for him and their children, and the bills are inevitably mounting.

If you ever laughed or shrieked at one of McInroy’s films or just want to help an Austin filmmaker in their hour of need, you can donate now via his GoFundMe page.

The Chronicle's first Culture Desk editor, Richard has reported on Austin's growing film production and appreciation scene for over a decade. A graduate of the universities of York, Stirling, and UT-Austin, a Rotten Tomatoes certified critic, and eight-time Best of Austin winner, he's currently at work on two books and a play.
